City Council
AGENDA
A REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
October 21, 2013
07:00 P.M.
City Hall Council Chambers
24300 Narbonne Avenue
1.
OPENING CEREMONIES
a.
Call Meeting to Order
b.
Flag Salute
c.

d.

2.
APPROVAL OF AGENDA
3.
PRESENTATIONS
Proclamation declaring October 24, 2013, as World Polio Day in the City of Lomita.
4.
ORAL COMMUNICATIONS Persons wishing to speak on Consent Agenda items or subjects other than those scheduled are requested to do so at this time. In order to conduct a timely meeting, a 5 minute time limit per person has been established. Amendments to Government Code Section 54954.2 prohibit the Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda.
5.
ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE CITY COUNCIL The City Council may discuss and act upon items described under Council Comments; however, items which are not will be limited to Council reports, announcements, or requests for clarification, or factual information, or to placement of matters on the agenda for a future meeting.

7.
CONSENT AGENDA
All items under the Consent Agenda are considered by the Council to be routine and will be enacted by one motion in the form listed below. There may be separate discussions of these items prior to the time the Council votes on the motion. Specific items may be removed from the Consent Agenda at the request of any Councilmember or staff.

Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Special City Council Meeting held on October 7, 2013, and the Regular City Council Meeting held on October 7, 2013. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

RECOMMEND APPROVAL
Staff report- item 7.E
PUBLIC HEARING:
8.
APPEAL OF CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT NO. 281 Discussion, review and appeal of the Planning Commission's decision regarding Conditional Use Permit No. 281 located at 25114-8 Narbonne Avenue, Lomita in the C-G (Commercial General) Zone. The proposed project is a mixed-use development consisting of 8 residential units and 2,900 square feet of commercial floor area. Staff recommends that the City Council adopt a resolution upholding the Planning Commission's decision approving the project.
Presented by Assistant City Manager Sugano
Staff Report- item 8
ADJOURNMENT
Written materials distributed to the City Council within 72 hours of the City Council meeting are available for public inspection immediately upon distribution in the City Clerk's office at 24300 Narbonne Avenue.
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, you should contact the office of the City Clerk at 310 325-7110 (voice) or the California Relay Service. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the city to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility to this meeting.
minutes_text:
MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
October 21, 2013

1.  OPENING CEREMONIES

a.  Call Meeting to Order

A regular meeting of the Lomita City Council was called to order at 7:00 p.m., on
Monday, October 21, 2013, in the Council Chambers, at Lomita City Hall, 24300
Narbonne Avenue.

b.  Flag Salute

Councilmember Sanchez led the salute to the flag.

c.  Invocation

Councilmember Traina gave the invocation.

d.  Roll Call

Those responding to roll call by Assistant City Clerk Shumway were
COUNCILMEMBERS: Gazeley, Traina, Savidan, Sanchez, and Mayor Estrada. Also
present were City Manager Rock, Assistant City Manager Sugano, City Attorney Hogin,
Community Services Director McPherron, Parks and Recreation Director Harding, and
Assistant City Clerk Shumway.

2.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA

Councilmember Gazeley moved to approve the agenda.  Councilmember Savidan
seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

3.  PRESENTATIONS

Mayor Estrada read a proclamation and declared Thursday, October 24, 2013, as World
Polio Day in the City of Lomita. Richard Kawasaki, member of the Lomita-Torrance
Airport Rotary Club, stated that polio has been eradicated almost completely throughout
the world, except for three countries. Mr. Kawasaki also thanked City Council for
recognizing and helping the cause.

4. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

Joe McGrath, Lomita resident, stated that the information provided by the City

  Page 1
 contradicts information posted on the Metropolitan Water District’s website regarding
water hardness, and use of ground water and well water. Mr. McGrath stated that
Metropolitan water comes from the Colorado River and the State Project, and that no
ground or well water is used by Metropolitan. In addition, Mr. McGrath pointed out that
during the month of May 2013, there were several shutdowns at the Cypress Water
Production Facility of which residents were not informed about. Mr. McGrath further
expressed his concern about the quality of water in Lomita, and requested more
transparency and openness from the City regarding this issue.

Marty Spain, Lomita resident, pointed out that the City’s Administrative Services
Department has seven employees, with total salaries budgeted at $527,228, and that
38% of those salaries are being charged to the Water Fund. Mr. Spain asked City
Council to review the total number of City employees.

Scott Mann, Lomita resident, stated that Alta Vista Street has never been resurfaced,
and asked how he could request a future agenda item in order to discuss the possibility
of resurfacing the street, to which City Manager Rock responded by informing Mr. Mann
to contact Public Works Director Damasse.

Mike Graf, Lomita resident, recommended that City Council both review and change the
procedure regarding how items get placed on future agendas in order to make it less
strict.

George Kivett, Lomita resident, agreed with Mr. Graf about making the process of
placing items on the agenda easier. Mr. Kivett also suggested that bottled water be
offered to members of the public during City Council meetings. Furthermore, Mr. Kivett
stated that recently the smell of chlorine in Lomita’s water has increased. And lastly, Mr.
Kivett requested that the crosswalk at Narbonne Avenue be fixed.

Barry Waite, Lomita resident and Former City Councilmember, requested that residents
remain civil and keep things in perspective, as the City election will be over in two
weeks. Mr. Waite also thanked City Council for all their work.

Cindy Segawa, Lomita resident, stated that she was concerned about the
misrepresentation of the PTA organization, in which a campaigning organization was
similarly named. Ms. Segawa stated that that was very misleading, and that the PTA
does not endorse any candidate. Ms. Segawa referenced the Fair Campaign Practices
Code, as well as the City’s mission statement, and requested that all City
Councilmember candidates operate with the utmost integrity and to not use deceptive
campaign practices.

Robert Knight, Lomita resident, asked that City Council drink tap water during Council

  Page 2
 meetings, instead of bottled water.

Mark Waronek, Lomita resident, invited those in attendance to the Annual Pancake
Breakfast for the Kiwanis Club on Sunday, November 3, 2013, from 7:00 a.m. to 12:00
p.m.

James Thompson, Lomita resident, stated that the entire City Council voted to start
water blending, and that the State of California regulatory departments granted the City
permission to start water blending. The City’s water passed all drinking water quality
and health standards. Furthermore, Mr. Thompson referred to the last three months’
water quality and testing reports, and stated that the City has reduced its dependency
on imported water from Metropolitan tremendously, and that there are no hazardous
materials or chemicals in Lomita’s water. Lastly, Mr. Thompson stated that the water
quality in Lomita is good, with no issues, and he went on to commend all the
Councilmembers for making the decision to start water blending.

5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE
  CITY COUNCIL

Councilmember Traina requested a future agenda item to discuss street sweeping in
cul-de-sacs. Councilmembers Gazeley and Sanchez agreed to have the discussion
item placed on a future City Council agenda.

Councilmember Traina requested a future agenda item to reconsider how items are
placed on the agenda, and to potentially change the current policy of requiring consent
from three Councilmembers in order for items to be placed on a future agenda.
Councilmembers Sanchez and Gazeley agreed to have this discussion item placed on a
future Council agenda.

Councilmember Traina stated that at the last Council meeting he was informed that the
flushing of fire hydrants was routine maintenance, and inquired as to whether any tests
were performed during the recent flushing, to which City Manager Rock responded that
no tests were performed.

Councilmember Traina asked that Lomita voters vote with their conscience.

Councilmember Sanchez reported that on Saturdays, members of the Community
Emergency Response Team (CERT) Committee meet in City Hall, and he also
reminded residents that they can sign-up for an upcoming CERT training, as well as an
upcoming refresher training for currently certified CERT members.

Councilmember Sanchez clarified that when crews are doing any major road work, or

  Page 3
 putting in new water lines, fire hydrants need to be flushed regularly. Councilmember
Sanchez also requested that staff fix the crosswalk at Narbonne Avenue.

Councilmember Savidan also requested that staff fix the crosswalk at Narbonne
Avenue, and asked that the Sheriff’s Department do an operation/enforcement sting at
that crosswalk, as drivers currently violate posted signs and do not yield to pedestrians.

Councilmember Gazeley also agreed that the crosswalk at Narbonne Avenue needs to
be fixed. Furthermore, Councilmember Gazeley reported that he attended the Los
Angeles/Orange County Jobs and Labor Summit on October 16, 2013, and the Greater
Los Angeles Water Summit on October 17, 2013. Councilmember Gazeley also
reported that by 2020, Metropolitan water would consist of one third Colorado River
water and State Project water, with the remaining two thirds coming from ground water
and recycled water.

Mayor Estrada reported that she also attended the Greater Los Angeles Water Summit,
which she stated was very good. Furthermore, Mayor Estrada announced that West
Basin’s 15th Annual Water Harvest Festival is scheduled for Saturday, October 26,
2013, and will take place in El Segundo. Lastly, Mayor Estrada invited those in
attendance to the Lomita Sister City fundraising event at Alfredo’s restaurant, from 9
a.m. to dinner time.

6.  CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

City Manager Rock stated that for the last two weeks residents have received 100%
Metropolitan water, as the transformer at the Cypress Water Production Facility failed
and needed to be replaced by Edison.

City Manager Rock provided an overview of legislative bills that were recently passed
and signed by the Governor, which included: AB 327, authorizing the State Public
Utilities Commission to come up with a new formula aimed at lowering electric bills for
people living in the warmer parts of the state, while raising them for those living in the
more moderate coastal climates; SB 333, allowing fines, up to the full cost of a
response, for people convicted of falsely reporting emergencies to 911; AB 370,
requiring new privacy policy disclosures for websites regarding behavioral tracking and
personal information collected; and AB 66, making utility companies disclose outages.
City Manager Rock concluded his overview by stating that there will be another bill
coming up in the future that would require utility companies to pay affected customers
for damages resulting from power outages.

  Page 4
 7. CONSENT AGENDA

Councilmember Traina moved to approve the Consent Agenda.  Councilmember
Savidan seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

  a. Motion to Waive Further Reading

  b. Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Special City Council Meeting held
  on October 7, 2013, and the Regular City Council Meeting held on October 7,
  2013. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  c. Approval of Demands

  d. Monthly Report from the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department. RECEIVE
  AND FILE.

  e. Adopt an Ordinance amending the City of Lomita Zoning Map from C-R
  (Commercial-Retail), to R-1 (Single Family Residential) for the properties located
  at 25816 Walnut Street, 25829 Appian Way, and 25829 ¼ Appian Way; and adopt
  an Ordinance amending Section 11-1.48.04 of the Lomita Municipal Code to allow
  “parking lots and parking buildings” as a conditionally permitted use in the C-R
  (Commercial-Retail), Zone. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  PUBLIC HEARING:

6. APPEAL OF CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT NO. 281

Assistant City Manager Sugano provided a PowerPoint presentation (Attachment 1),
and stated that a Conditional Use Permit (CUP) is required for all new mixed-use
projects. According to Assistant City Manager Sugano, the project in question meets all
development standards, with the exception of the size of the commercial floor area,
which could be amended as part of the CUP process. Assistant City Manager Sugano
continued by providing an overview of the proposed site plan, and recommended that
City Council adopt a resolution upholding the Planning Commission’s decision
approving the CUP.

Discussion followed regarding the width of the plot, and how the commercial area
minimum requirements are calculated.

In response to Councilmember Sanchez’s question about how the parking requirements
were calculated, as he believed there would not be enough parking to accommodate
certain types of business, Assistant City Manager Sugano responded that the
development is planned for specific uses, and such uses will be limited to ensure
compliance with parking code requirements. Assistant City Manager Sugano added
that staff is currently expecting that the majority of the commercial area will be utilized
for general office space.

  Page 5
 Mehrzad Givechi, the development project applicant, stated that the previously
approved CUP was not financially feasible, and therefore, the project was changed to
meet the existing mixed-use overlay.

Mayor Estrada opened the Public Hearing.

George Kivett, Lomita resident, stated that the proposed development project is good,
fits well with existing infrastructure, and would bring new commercial frontage to
Narbonne Avenue. Mr. Kivett recommended that Council approval of the project.

Mayor Estrada closed the Public Hearing.

Councilmember Sanchez stated that he requested an appeal of the Planning
Commission’s decision regarding CUP No. 281, based on two reasons: first being
concern over further reduction in commercial property space requirements, which were
reduced by 10%, and additional reduction of such space requirements through the CUP
could possibly reduce the overall size of revenue generating commercial properties in
the City; and the second reason dealt with limited parking for the proposed development
project.

Councilmember Savidan stated that this will be the first development project since the
mixed-use overlay for Narbonne Avenue and Lomita Boulevard was approved, and that
the success of this project might bring in other developers with similar projects.
Councilmember Savidan moved to approve the recommendation of staff.
Councilmember Gazeley seconded the motion.

ROLL CALL:
AYES: Councilmember Savidan, Gazeley, Traina, and Mayor Estrada
NOES: Councilmember Sanchez

ADJOURNMENT

Meeting adjourned at 8:09 p.m.

Respectfully Submitted,

__________________________________
Lena Shumway, Assistant City Clerk, CMC
